title.value: Global SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardized population-based studies from Jan 2020-May 2022
title.justification: The paper's title accurately reflects the contents, which include a systematic review and meta-analysis of worldwide seroprevalence data related to SARS-CoV-2.
title.quote: Global SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardized population-based studies from Jan 2020-May 2022

extractions.description: This paper conducts a systematic review and meta-analysis on global SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence studies conducted from January 2020 to May 2022. The study estimates changes in global and regional infection rates and examines case under-ascertainment by comparing seroprevalence with confirmed cases. It highlights the importance of standardized seroprevalence studies, especially in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), to better inform COVID-19 response efforts.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is primarily focused on understanding the seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 globally, which, while important for public health, does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our understanding of the global scale of SARS-CoV-2 infection remains incomplete: routine surveillance data underestimates infection and cannot infer on population immunity, there is a predominance of asymptomatic infections, and uneven access to diagnostics.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not have a central theme related to climate or ecological sustainable development, as it focuses on the SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence results and their implications for public health.
primary_category.quote: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized seroprevalence studies worldwide aligned with the SEROPREV protocol, regardless of whether the study received support from WHO.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development in the paper, as it entirely focuses on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence studies.
secondary_categories.quote: Our estimates of infections based on seroprevalence far exceed reported COVID-19 cases. Quality and standardized seroprevalence studies are essential to inform COVID-19 response, particularly in resource-limited regions.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not delve into any sub-category of climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: Seroprevalence studies estimate the prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 antibodies.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: This paper has no focus on any secondary sub-categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: In this study, we observed that global seroprevalence has risen considerably over time and with regional variation, however around 40 % of the global population remains susceptible to SARS-CoV-2 infection.

applications.value: Understanding the global seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection to improve public health interventions and response strategies.
applications.justification: This emphasizes the paper's focus on synthesizing seroprevalence data to better understand SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and improve public health responses.
applications.quote: Standardized seroprevalence studies are essential to inform COVID-19 response, particularly in resource-limited regions.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not identify any new categories or areas directly related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: Our findings provide evidence of regional and temporal variation in the overall seroprevalence, over 80% in SEAR and AFR in late 2021 and over 90% in AMR HIC and EUR HIC in early 2022.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus remains on SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence without venturing into unlisted sub-categories under climate or ecological sustainable development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Seroprevalence studies have been invaluable throughout the COVID-19 pandemic to understand the true extent and dynamics over time of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
